props.title: Pickup on South Street
props.initialSlug: Noir about a pickpocket caught in Cold War intrigue

sections.content: Samuel Fuller's **Pickup on South Street** (1953) revolutionized film noir by injecting raw street energy into Cold War paranoia. Richard Widmark's Skip McCoy, a magnetic pickpocket who accidentally lifts microfilm meant for Communist agents, represents noir's perfect anti-hero - cynical, self-serving, yet ultimately redeemable. Fuller's aggressive camera movements and gritty New York locations created a template followed by later crime films like **The French Connection** (1971) and **Mean Streets** (1973).

sections.content: The film's portrayal of informants and street life, particularly through Thelma Ritter's unforgettable performance as stool pigeon Moe Williams, influenced countless crime dramas. Her character's tragic dignity elevated the archetype beyond simple plot device, echoing through films like **The Departed** (2006) and **Donnie Brasco** (1997). Fuller's documentary-style approach to New York's underground economy created a visceral realism that distinguished it from more stylized noirs like **Double Indemnity** (1944).

Jean Peters' conflicted performance as Candy brings unexpected depth to the noir femme fatale archetype. Unlike the calculating women of **Out of the Past** (1947) or **The Maltese Falcon** (1941), Candy is a working-class character caught between loyalty and survival. This more nuanced approach to female characters in noir influenced later films like **Chinatown** (1974) and **L.A. Confidential** (1997). SUBHEAD: Cold War Noir

movies.title: The Big Heat
movies.slug: A tough cop takes on corruption after his wife is killed by mobsters

sections.content: Fuller's integration of Cold War themes with street-level crime created a distinct noir sub-genre that influenced films like **The Third Man** (1949) and **North by Northwest** (1959). The film's unflinching look at patriotism through the lens of self-interest feels startlingly modern, predating similar themes in **Three Days of the Condor** (1975) and **The Good Shepherd** (2006).
